verdict: Martin Marietta's sales jumped 28% after its August combination with Lhoist North America transformed its lime business — but profit fell 38% to $256M as interest costs more than doubled and margins thinned.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +28% YoY, mostly the Lhoist North America deal

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $5.97 from continuing operations a year ago

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: vs 33.1% a year ago — mix shift to acquired volumes

kpis.label: Interest expense
kpis.note: up from $59M — debt taken on for the combination

segments.name: Building Materials — East
segments.note: Aggregates (crushed stone, sand and gravel), cement and concrete in the eastern U.S. — operating earnings actually fell to $312M from $335M as volumes and pricing softened.

segments.name: Building Materials — West
segments.note: The western building-materials business — Texas, Colorado, California and Arizona — boosted by acquisitions.

segments.name: Specialties
segments.note: Lime and magnesia chemicals for steel, water treatment and industry. Revenue is against a recast year-ago figure (part of the old business moved to discontinued operations); the Lhoist deal, closed August 21, made Martin Marietta the nation's leading lime producer.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Sales and back office for the quarry and plant network.

opex.name: Acquisition & integration, net
opex.note: $84M of acquisition, divestiture and integration expenses (mostly the Lhoist combination), less $4M of other operating income.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $138M — up from $59M a year ago on debt for the Lhoist deal — partly offset by $13M of other nonoperating income.
oneTimers: $84M of acquisition, divestiture and integration expenses tied mainly to the Lhoist North America combination, which closed August 21, 2026.

takeaways.title: The Lhoist deal reshaped the company
takeaways.text: Combining with Lhoist North America made Martin Marietta the nation's leading producer of lime and limestone products. Specialties posted record revenue of $362M, including only five weeks of Lhoist.

takeaways.title: Growth diluted margins — for now
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell to 27.5% from 33.1%: acquired volumes carry lower margins and the core East aggregates business earned less ($312M vs $335M) on softer shipments.

takeaways.title: Leverage is the bill for growth
takeaways.text: Interest expense more than doubled to $138M and the share count rose about 8% on stock issued for the deal — together they turned +28% revenue growth into a 34% drop in continuing EPS.

footerNote: All figures are from continuing operations; this quarter had no discontinued-operations earnings (the year-ago quarter had $53M). Martin Marietta does not allocate the items between segment operating earnings ($560M) and reported operating earnings ($438M) in the release beyond corporate costs and the acquisition charges shown.
